essential: Washington's task of controlling planetary New York. The forces are aligned only in foreign affairs.
Hay at his summit on the edge of wreck over China's open door. Herbert succeeds Pauncefote, and friendship reduces friction.
The Kaiser recalls Holleben and sends Speck von Sternburg. Germany swings west, which isolates Cassini and leaves Hay's problem as Russia alone. Adams's admiration for this 'paradox'.

Russia as the enigma. Adams has personal reasons for goodwill (Alexander I and J. Q. Adams; Alexander II in 1862). His hope that Russia joins the combine within sixty years. Cassini's transparent emotion and Russia's fatal rolling.
Russia plus China forms one undeflectable mass. The insect's chart of spring 1903 shows the open door failing and the game seemingly lost. Present this as Adams's forecast then, not as fact.
The inertia questions: volume against intensity, vis nova against vis inertiae. His redefinition of mental inertia as movement round habitual motives.
Minds are unequally inert. Race-inertia is constant. Sex-inertia has never been overcome; maternity is the unbroken sequence; Americans ignore sex.
Early Women became a passion. The dinner-table trick and its answer. The May 1903 farewell dinner with the named guests, in which Adams's speech names each superior wife; the men laugh a little.
The clever woman's bitterness: the family dissolved, no place in Church or State, motherhood over at forty.

Artificial energy has been turned over to the American woman. She has been volatilized like a perfect gas, with millions of new working women. Can inertia take direction except along lines of inertia?
She follows the man, whose hand is on the lever. She becomes sexless and must marry machinery. Religion is the old refuge; the Church was a woman's protest.
The historian cannot take sides and can learn only from the birth-rate. Ironic proposals (census, Senate law). Faust is helpless. Ending: Russia seems easier than America; the horseshoe crab retreat.

voice_profile: Third-person self-portrait in which 'Adams', 'the student', 'the historian', 'the insect' or 'the gray-headed moth' is mocked by his own narrator. The prose is ironic and aphoristic. Each paragraph builds a long periodic sentence through dashes and semicolons toward a deflating epigram. Adams compulsively converts persons and politics into physics: force, inertia, attraction, mass, acceleration and the 'larger synthesis'. He constantly professes ignorance, and that ignorance is itself the method. Paradox is treated as orthodoxy. Learned allusions (Seneca, Pascal, Aquinas, Lucretius, Faust) are deployed with self-deprecating humour. Quotations from real sources are marked and attributed. Double hyphens and French or Latin tags are part of the texture.
